passage.title: Some People Leave Us More
paras: Some people leave us money. Some people leave us houses. The best people leave us something we can carry for ever: a way of living. My grandfather left me his patience; my teacher left me her love of words; my neighbour left me the habit of saying salaam to everyone in the street. We remember them not for what they owned, not for what they won, but for what they gave.

model.title: Write three parallel sentences about hope.

parts.text: Choose a pattern: Hope is the...
Fill it three times with different images
Read aloud to check the rhythm

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Hope is the light at the end of the road. Hope is the hand that lifts us up. Hope is the story we refuse to stop telling.

using the same grammatical pattern in a row

questions.q: Identify the device: 'Not for fame, not for money, but for the people.'
questions.a: Parallelism (not for... not for... but for...) with repetition of 'for'

questions.q: Add a third parallel clause: 'We remember the lost, we honour the brave, ...'

Core: in the portal response box, write a short paragraph (five sentences) for a school assembly about remembering people who made a difference, using one repetition and one set of three parallel phrases. Starter: 'Some people leave us...'
questions.a: A paragraph with deliberate repetition and parallelism; strongest idea last.

questions.q: Extend: label each device in the margin
Stretch: explain why too much repetition can weaken writing
questions.a: It can sound dull or forced; repetition works best when it is rare and deliberate.

options: Reading is good and also writing.

questions.a: B) We read to learn, we write to share, we speak to change.. Three clauses follow the same pattern: we + verb + to + verb.

questions.q: 'We came, we saw, we learned' is an example of...
Answer the ponder: why does a matching pattern stick in the memory?
questions.a: For example: rhythm and balance make it easy to hear and remember.
